sites_touched_JUDGEMENT: 3 files: guard moved out of set.ts into a shared module and applied at 4 reference sites in references.ts (root context lookup, property read, index access, method call); two `in` tests replaced by own-property tests
sibling_sites_exist_JUDGEMENT: yes: every way a template can walk from a value to its prototype chain
entry_point_GUESS: Library API: rendering an attacker-controlled Velocity template (property read reaching the Function constructor)
flaw_one_line: The guard added for GHSA-j658-c2gf-x6pq blocks constructor / __proto__ / prototype only in #set assignment paths; property reads and method calls are unfiltered, so a template can reach the Function constructor and execute code.
tempting_wrong_fix_JUDGEMENT: Block the key 'constructor' in the one property-read path the proof of concept uses. Index access, method calls and the root context lookup stay open; and banning the key names outright also hides legitimate own properties called 'constructor', which the real fix keeps readable through an own-property test.
why_hard_or_why_control_JUDGEMENT: S3 and S4: a guard for exactly these keys exists and the advisory is a stated bypass of it. S1: the same rule has to be applied at every reference-resolution path (4 sites plus the #set paths). S7: a keyword ban breaks data objects that have such keys as own properties.
caveats: TypeScript, the models' strongest language, and a code-injection class; kept because signals 1, 3, 4 and 7 all apply. Small project (615 stars).
